newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Patents on medicines linked to marketing rights - Court.
newsitem.headline: Patents on medicines linked to marketing rights - Court.

text.p: The European Court of Justice found on Thursday that supplementary certificates to extend patent protection on medicines are strictly linked to an existing market authorization in a member state.
Ciba-Geigy was denied marketing approval in Britain in 1989 for its inhaled anti-asthma formulation eformoterol due to special storage conditions required, according to court documents.

The drug was covered by a patent in Britain however, and two days before it was to expire, the holder of the patent sought a supplementary protection certificate from British authorities to extend the patent.
The application was rejected for lack of a valid authorization to place the product on the market.
When the British authorites denied the certificate, Yamanouchi Pharmaceuticals, the patent owner, challenged that decision on the basis of European Union harmonised rules on patents for medicines.

"Entitlement to the certificate is strictly linked to the existence of a marketing authorization granted in the member state in which the application is submitted and to the date of that application," the court said.
Reference for a preliminary ruling by the High Court of Justice, Chancery Division, Patents Court in the proceedings between
Comptroller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks
on the interpretation of article 19 of Council regulation (EEC) No 1768/92 concerning the creation of a supplementary protection certificate for medicinal products (OJ 1992 L 182, p. 1)

The grant of a supplementary protection certificate pursuant to article 19 of Council regulation (EEC) No 1768/92 concerning the creation of a supplementary protection certificate for medicinal products is, in accordance with article 3(b) of that regulation, conditional on a valid authorization to place the product on the market as a medicinal product having been granted in the member state in which the application is submitted and at the date of that application.
